title: Data Structures & Algorithms
description: Build durable problem-solving skills through concepts, deterministic traces, Java practice, and adaptive feedback.

concepts.title: Arrays
concepts.explanation: Arrays store fixed-size elements in contiguous positions. Indices make random access constant time; insertion or deletion in the middle requires shifting elements.
examples: Use two pointers from both ends

concepts.title: Strings
concepts.summary: Sequences of characters and pattern operations
concepts.explanation: Treat strings as character sequences. Many string problems reduce to array traversal, frequency maps, or two-pointer windows.

concepts.title: Linked Lists
concepts.explanation: A linked list stores values in nodes linked by references. Local insertion is constant time when the node is known, while indexed access is linear.

concepts.title: Stacks
concepts.explanation: A stack exposes push, pop, and peek. It models nested work and reversible history.

concepts.title: Queues
concepts.explanation: Queues process elements in arrival order. A circular buffer avoids repeated shifting.

concepts.title: Recursion
concepts.explanation: A recursive function needs a base case and progress toward it. The call stack retains unfinished work.

concepts.title: Searching
concepts.explanation: Linear search scans candidates. Binary search discards half of a sorted search interval after each comparison.

concepts.title: Sorting
concepts.summary: Arrange values by a comparison rule
concepts.explanation: Sorting algorithms differ in time, memory, stability, and adaptiveness. Understand their invariants rather than memorising code.

concepts.title: Trees
concepts.explanation: Trees model hierarchy. Binary search trees order keys; traversals expose nodes in depth-first or breadth-first order.

concepts.title: Graphs
concepts.explanation: Graphs represent general relationships. BFS explores layers; DFS follows paths. Visited state prevents repeated work.

concepts.title: Hashing
concepts.explanation: Hash tables map keys to buckets. Performance depends on distribution, load factor, and collision handling.
